summary: ESA first-party map and service routes were inspected after separate English and Arabic discovery. They document request-based digital mapping and surveying, but no anonymous Bilbeis parcel ID plus geometry response was verified. This is not evidence of citywide cadastral absence.
queryOutcomes: Both discovery queries and actual result URLs are recorded in city-6699-bilbeis.json.
requestOutcomes: ESA services, digital-map workflow, historical-map catalog and testmap GETs returned 200; current HTML/scripts exposed no public parcel feature service. Sharqia bulletin was treated as administrative context only.
scopeLimits: No city boundary or complete Bilbeis coverage was established.
No exact-point hit/miss was used as an absence claim.
No parcel geometry or source-specific attributes were retained.
General national-agency prose and governorate statistics are not treated as proof of a local open registry adapter.
No credentials, login, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, owner/address/titleholder/tax fields, or private tokens were used.
nativeIdentityPolicy: No native parcel identity was observed; no synthetic identity was created. A future retained sample must use exactly one stable native identity and keep native field mapping/composite-key provenance in metadata.
serialReviewerQualification: not qualified; independent serial review still required
uncertainty: The national map custodian and local administrative context are evidenced, but anonymous parcel access, city scope, schema, CRS, stable native IDs and geometry remain unknown.
